payload.reason: The evidence provides a comparison of the adaptively sparse Transformer method against standard softmax Transformers and other variants, indicating performance metrics and qualitative improvements.

claims.text: The adaptively sparse Transformer improves interpretability and head diversity compared to softmax Transformers, showing that heads in different layers learn different sparsity preferences.
Replacing softmax with entmax does not hurt performance; sparse attention Transformers tend to achieve slightly higher BLEU scores.
The end-to-end computational overhead of the adaptively sparse methods is relatively small, achieving 75% and 90% of the training speed of the softmax model.
Sparse Transformer variants exhibit more diversity in attention heads compared to traditional softmax models, particularly in the middle layers of the encoder self-attention.
